title: 1956 AHSME Problem 46
statement: For the equation \(\dfrac{1+x}{1-x}=\dfrac{N+1}{N}\) to be true where \(N\) is positive, \(x\) can have:

solutions.text:
Cross-multiplication gives \[ N(1+x)=(N+1)(1-x), \] so \(x(2N+1)=1\) and \[ x=\frac1{2N+1}. \] Every positive \(N\) gives \(0\lt x\lt1.\) Conversely, for any \(0\lt x\lt1,\) \[ N=\frac{1-x}{2x}>0, \] so such an \(N\) exists.

Thus, \(x\) may be any positive value less than \(1,\) and the correct answer is A.
hints: Cross-multiply and solve for \(x\) in terms of \(N\)
The equation reduces to \(x=\frac{1}{2N+1};\) also solve this relation for \(N\)
